summary: Describes an architectural framework for network telemetry, which gathers network insight for efficient and automated management. It covers data generation, collection, correlation, and consumption, clarifies terms, and classifies the components of a telemetry system. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A guide to how a network can report on its own health and how those reports are gathered and used.

questions: what are the network telemetry modules
subtitle: A common map of network telemetry: four modules, five components and four kinds of data, so that existing and future techniques have a place to fit.

tldr.problem: Networks need to supply much more, and much fresher, data to automated tools than polling-based OAM such as SNMP, CLI and Syslog can provide, and the term network telemetry had no clear definition.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC splits telemetry into four modules (management, control, forwarding and external data), breaks each into five components, and classifies data as simple, derived, event-triggered or streaming.
tldr.outcome: It defines no new protocol. It gives a shared taxonomy and maps existing mechanisms such as YANG-Push, gNMI, BMP, IPFIX and IOAM onto it.

today: RFC 9232 is an Informational RFC from the IETF, published in May 2022. The unit metadata shows no RFC obsoletes or updates it, and it defines no protocol of its own.

sections.title: Why a Telemetry Framework
sections.content:
Network telemetry covers both the data about the state of a network and the techniques used to generate, export, collect and consume it, often for automated management applications. The RFC says it extends beyond classical Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) and expects better flexibility, scalability, accuracy, coverage and performance.

Operators have long relied on SNMP, the command-line interface and Syslog. The RFC lists why these fall short: low-frequency polling suits continuous monitoring poorly, their data coverage is narrow, some lack a formal data model, their push options are limited to predefined warnings or sampled packets, and conventional passive and active measurement either waste resources or disturb traffic.

The RFC is explicit that it does not define specific technologies. Its purpose is to set common ground and guide later work.
sections.eli5: Old ways of checking on a network are like asking a friend for an update once in a while. Telemetry is more like the friend texting you every time something changes.

sections.title: Applicability and Privacy Limits
sections.content:
The RFC warns that large-scale network data collection is a major threat to user privacy and may be indistinguishable from pervasive monitoring (RFC 7258). The framework must not be applied to generating, collecting, analyzing or retaining individual user data, or data that can identify end users or characterize their behavior without consent.

For that reason it is not applicable to networks whose endpoints are individual users, such as general-purpose access networks. It suits contexts such as industrial, data-center and infrastructure networks. Telemetry should also not include packet payload from end-user traffic.
sections.eli5: The rule is to watch the roads, not to read people's mail.

sections.title: Four Modules and Five Components
sections.content:
The top level splits telemetry by where the data comes from, because the source decides the export location, data model, encoding and transport. There are four modules:

  • Management plane telemetry: configuration and operational state, using SNMP, syslog, NETCONF, RESTCONF and gRPC.
  • Control plane telemetry: health of control protocols such as BGP or IS-IS. The BGP Monitoring Protocol (BMP) is the example given.
  • Forwarding plane telemetry: flow, packet, queue and table data from forwarding chips, with IPFIX and traffic mirroring as examples.
  • External data telemetry: events outside the network, such as sensors, news reports and global event analyzers.

Each module is built from the same five components: data query, analysis and storage; data configuration and subscription; data encoding and export; data generation and processing; and data object and source. The RFC stresses that no universal protocol can cover every requirement, since a forwarding chip has high throughput but little processing capacity, while a control CPU is the opposite.
sections.eli5: There are four kinds of watchers: ones looking at the rules, the road signs, the cars and the weather. Each has the same five jobs, from spotting things to filing the reports.

sections.title: How Data Is Acquired and Classified
sections.content:
Data can be acquired by subscription (push) or query (poll). A subscription is a contract between publisher and subscriber, and data keeps arriving until it expires. Queries give immediate, one-off answers and suit interactive applications.

The RFC names four types of data a consumer can subscribe to or query:

  • Simple data: steadily available from a datastore or static probe.
  • Derived data: synthesized in the network from raw data.
  • Event-triggered data: acquired when something happens, such as an interface changing state.
  • Streaming data: continuously generated, such as a packet counter exported every second, and always pushed.

These types are not mutually exclusive. Derived data is composed of simple data, and event-triggered and streaming data can build on both.
sections.eli5: You can ask a question and get one answer, or sign up for updates. The updates can be plain facts, worked-out facts, news when something happens, or a never-ending stream.

sections.title: Telemetry Techniques and Their Trade-offs
sections.content:
The RFC classifies forwarding plane techniques along several axes. Passive methods (IPFIX, sFlow, mirroring) usually have low data coverage, or cost high bandwidth to raise it. Active methods (Ping, OWAMP, TWAMP, STAMP) are intrusive and give only indirect measurements. Hybrid methods such as IOAM and Alternate Marking balance the two but are more complex to implement.

Data can also be in-band, carried in user packets as in IOAM, or out-of-band, exported directly without altering packets, as in the postcard-based approach. Subjects can be flow based, path based or node based.

Telemetry should avoid the "observer effect": it must not change network behavior or forwarding performance, and high-volume telemetry traffic needs isolation, traffic engineering or congestion control. Appendix A surveys examples, including YANG-Push, gNMI, BMP, Alternate Marking, IPFIX, IOAM and postcard-based telemetry.
sections.eli5: You can watch cars from the roadside, send a test car, or tape a note to real cars. Each way has costs, and none should cause a traffic jam.

sections.title: Evolution and Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC describes four stages of telemetry applications: Stage 0 static, Stage 1 dynamic, Stage 2 interactive and Stage 3 closed-loop, where no human is involved except for reports. It says existing technologies are ready for Stages 0 and 1, and a framework is the first step toward the later stages.

On security, telemetry data can be manipulated to exhaust resources, falsified data can mislead decisions, and the data itself is highly sensitive because it exposes details such as installed software and patches. Considerations include trust and policy models, role-based access control, transport security, data store protection, authentication and integrity of data, and separating telemetry traffic from data traffic. The RFC says further study of these issues is required.
sections.eli5: Telemetry can grow from fixed gauges to a system that watches and fixes the network itself. Because the reports are secret and powerful, they must be locked up and checked for tampering.

items.title: Simple data
items.text: Steadily available from a datastore or static probe.

items.title: Derived data
items.text: Synthesized or processed from raw data in the network.

items.title: Event-triggered data
items.text: Acquired when an event occurs, such as an interface going up or down.

items.title: Streaming data
items.text: Continuously generated and always pushed to subscribers.
